potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Ruler Braces
potential_solutions.description: Use the masking tape to attach the long wooden rulers to the outside edges of the cereal boxes as you stack them. The stiff rulers will hold the boxes straight and stop them from folding in the wind.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Yarn Anchors
potential_solutions.description: Tape one end of the yarn to the higher boxes of your tower, and tape the other end tightly to the floor of your fort. This acts like tent strings holding your tower steady from all sides.

title: The Flying Marble Mystery
complaint: Hi! I'm Stella. I am building a giant marble run in my backyard treehouse, but every time the marble hits the big cardboard curve, it flies right off the track into the grass!

clue_cards.title: Bumper Power
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes things need a soft wall to bounce off of instead of just rolling over an open edge.

clue_cards.title: Slow It Down
clue_cards.insight: If a toy is moving too fast, adding a bumpy surface can help slow it down before it reaches a sharp turn.

clue_cards.title: Banking the Turn
clue_cards.insight: Think about toy car race tracks! Tilting the track inward on corners helps keep things from flying out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Clay Bumper
potential_solutions.description: Stick a big lump of modeling clay on the outside edge of the curve. It acts like a soft wall to catch the fast marble and gently bump it back onto the track.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Rubber Band Speed Bumps
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a few rubber bands around the cardboard tube right before the curve. This creates little bumps that safely slow the marble down before it turns.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Tilted Track
potential_solutions.description: Use popsicle sticks and masking tape to prop up the outside edge of the cardboard curve so it leans inward, keeping the marble safely inside just like a real race track.

title: The Flying Marble Mystery
complaint: Hi! I'm Gabriel. I'm building a giant marble run in my backyard treehouse, but every time the marble hits the big bottom curve, it flies right off the track and gets lost in the grass!

clue_cards.title: Wall It Up
clue_cards.insight: If things are flying off the edge, they might need a tall barrier or a wall to bounce off safely.

clue_cards.title: Catch and Release
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes, instead of a sharp turn, you need to catch the rolling object first before dropping it onto a new path.

clue_cards.title: Slow It Down
clue_cards.insight: If an object is going too fast, making the path a little bumpy can help slow it down so it stays on track.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Bumper Wall
potential_solutions.description: Use the sticky tape to attach craft sticks around the outside edge of the big curve. This makes a tall wall that keeps the marble on the track as it goes around the bend.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Cup Catch
potential_solutions.description: Remove the sharp curve and tape the plastic cup at the end of the track instead. Poke a small hole in the bottom of the cup so the marble falls in, stops for a second, and drops straight down into the next tube.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Rubber Band Brakes
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a few rubber bands around the paper towel tubes right before the curve. This makes tiny bumps that act like brakes to slow the marble down just enough so it doesn't fly away!

title: The Windy Door Disaster
complaint: Hi! I'm Isaac. I am working in my backyard treehouse lab, but the strong wind keeps blowing my cardboard secret door wide open!
on_hand_items: A heavy bucket of toy blocks

clue_cards.title: Stretch and Snap
clue_cards.insight: Stretchy things want to shrink back to their normal size, which can help pull things shut.

clue_cards.title: Heavy Helpers
clue_cards.insight: A heavy object can act like a strong anchor to hold something in place if you tie them together.

clue_cards.title: Wedge It In
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes a long, stiff object can be jammed into a tight spot to stop something from moving.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Stretchy Door Closer
potential_solutions.description: Loop the large rubber bands together to make a stretchy chain. Attach one end to the door and the other to the wall inside, so it constantly pulls the door shut on its own.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Bucket Anchor
potential_solutions.description: Tie the jump rope to the door handle, toss the rope over a sturdy roof beam, and tie the heavy bucket of blocks to the other end. The weight of the bucket will pull the door closed.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Broom Jam
potential_solutions.description: Stick the handle of the push broom under the door knob and press the brush part firmly against the floor to securely wedge the door shut from the inside.

title: The Overhead Angle
complaint: Hi! I'm Willow. I am at my home office desk trying to film a top-down craft video, but I do not have an overhead tripod and my phone keeps falling over when I try to prop it up.
on_hand_items: Tall desk lamp with a bendable neck

clue_cards.title: Heavy Anchors
clue_cards.insight: Heavy everyday objects can easily hold down a makeshift stand so it does not tip over while you work.

clue_cards.title: Stretch and Secure
clue_cards.insight: Rubber bands are perfect for strapping your phone tightly to another object without slipping or scratching the screen.

clue_cards.title: Bendable Frames
clue_cards.insight: A wire coat hanger is easy to bend by hand to create a custom shelf, loop, or hook for holding small devices.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Use the rubber bands to strap your phone securely to the head of the desk lamp, then bend the lamp's neck so the phone's camera points straight down at the desk.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger into a long shape, slide one end under the stack of heavy books to lock it flat on the desk, and use rubber bands to tie your phone to the other end hanging over your workspace.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Bend the coat hanger into a tight cradle for the phone, secure the phone inside with rubber bands so it will not slip out, and hang the hook directly over the bent neck of the desk lamp.

title: The Broken Camera Rig
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm setting up a makeshift overhead camera rig in my home office to film a product pitch video, but the plastic mount on my cheap tripod just snapped, and my smartphone keeps sliding out of place every time I try to angle it straight down over the desk.
on_hand_items: A stack of heavy hardcover books
A desk lamp with an adjustable neck

clue_cards.title: Weight and Balance
clue_cards.insight: You can use heavy, flat objects to anchor something that needs to stick out over an edge without it tipping over.

clue_cards.title: Bendable Support
clue_cards.insight: Thick metal wire can be bent into a custom shape to cradle an object securely without blocking the camera lens.

clue_cards.title: Repurposing Structures
clue_cards.insight: Look for things in the room that already have adjustable arms; they can hold other objects if you secure them tightly.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Book Edge Mount
potential_solutions.description: Place the smartphone flat on top of the tallest stack of hardcover books near the desk edge, letting just the camera lens peek over the side. Place another heavy book on top of the phone's back half to pin it down securely.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Lamp Arm Swap
potential_solutions.description: Unplug the desk lamp and use the duct tape to strap the smartphone safely to the back of the lamp head. Use the lamp's adjustable neck to bend and aim the phone camera exactly where you need it over the desk.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Cradle
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger into a tight U-shape that grips the sides of the phone, tape the hook end firmly to the broken tripod stand, and bend the wire to hold the phone at a downward angle.

title: The Top-Down Tumble
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm working at my messy desk trying to film a top-down video of my new craft project, but my phone keeps slipping and falling flat every time I try to balance it on my stack of books.

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Get a Grip
clue_cards.insight: Rubber clings tightly to smooth surfaces. Adding something rubbery to the edges of your phone can stop it from sliding off the books.

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: Bend and Shape
clue_cards.insight: Thick wire can be bent into custom shapes. A simple hook or cradle shape can hold flat objects securely in the air.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: Heavy Anchors
clue_cards.insight: Heavy objects are great for holding down lighter structures. Sticking your support to a heavy weight will keep it from tipping forward.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Rubber Band Sandwich
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a few rubber bands around the top and bottom edges of your phone. Place the phone between the two top books in your stack, letting the camera peek out. The rubber bands will grip the book covers and stop the phone from sliding out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Wire Cradle
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger into a long loop to cradle the phone. Stick the hook end of the hanger inside the heavy ceramic mug and secure it firmly with duct tape to anchor the base, pointing the wire loop out over your work area.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Book Overhang
potential_solutions.description: Slide the top hardcover book so it hangs halfway off the edge of the stack, directly over your craft space. Place the heavy ceramic mug on the back half of the book to hold it down, then simply use duct tape to stick your phone to the underside of the overhanging book.

title: The Clamp Catastrophe
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm in my garage workshop trying to finish a custom birdhouse. The problem is my only wood clamp just snapped, and I need something to hold these two freshly glued pieces of wood tightly together while they dry!

clue_cards.title: Gravity's Grip
clue_cards.insight: When you can't squeeze things from the sides, try pressing them from the top down using everyday heavy objects.

clue_cards.title: Elastic Energy
clue_cards.insight: Stretchable items naturally want to shrink back to their original size, which creates a constant squeezing force.

clue_cards.title: The Binding Method
clue_cards.insight: Wrapping something tightly in a spiral pattern can lock two loose pieces firmly into one solid shape.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Weight
potential_solutions.description: Lay the glued wood flat on the workbench and stack the heavy paint cans right on top of the joint to press the pieces together while they dry.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Rubber Band Squeeze
potential_solutions.description: Stretch the thick rubber bands around both pieces of wood. The bands will constantly pull inward, acting just like a clamp.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Tape Wrap
potential_solutions.description: Wrap the duct tape tightly around the two pieces of wood. Pull the tape as hard as you can while wrapping to make sure the joint is pulled closed.

title: The Whiteboard Wipeout
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm in my home office trying to finalize a huge pitch for my startup, but I accidentally wrote my entire presentation on the whiteboard using a permanent marker!

clue_cards.title: Like Dissolves Like
clue_cards.insight: Permanent marker ink needs a strong liquid like alcohol to break it apart and make it wet again.

clue_cards.title: The Ink Erase Trick
clue_cards.insight: Dry-erase markers actually have liquid ingredients in them that keep their own ink from sticking permanently to the board.

clue_cards.title: Gentle Scrubbing
clue_cards.insight: You need something soft but slightly textured to wipe up the ink without scratching the smooth surface of the whiteboard.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Direct Action
potential_solutions.description: Trace over the permanent marker lines with the dry-erase marker. The wet liquid in the dry-erase marker will mix with the permanent ink, letting you wipe it all away easily with a coffee filter.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Environmental Adaptation
potential_solutions.description: Squirt a generous amount of hand sanitizer onto a coffee filter and scrub the board. The alcohol in the sanitizer will melt away the permanent ink right off the surface.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Lateral Swap
potential_solutions.description: Spray a small amount of hairspray directly over the permanent marker text. The strong ingredients in the hairspray will break down the ink so you can quickly wipe it clean before it dries.
